summary: Rifaximin is a minimally absorbed, gut-selective antibiotic used for travelers' diarrhea (non-invasive E. coli), reduction of recurrence of overt hepatic encephalopathy, and irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhea (IBS-D). Its very low systemic absorption gives a favorable safety and interaction profile, though it should not be used for diarrhea with fever or blood.
indications: Travelers' diarrhea caused by non-invasive strains of Escherichia coli (adults and children >=12 years)
Reduction in risk of overt hepatic encephalopathy recurrence (adults)
Irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhea (IBS-D) in adults

dosage.d: 550 mg three times daily for 14 days
dosage.n: May retreat up to 2 times if recurrence

admin: May be taken with or without food
Do not use for travelers' diarrhea complicated by fever or bloody stools
Discontinue if diarrhea worsens or persists beyond 24-48 hours (travelers' diarrhea)
moa: A non-systemic rifamycin that binds the beta-subunit of bacterial DNA-dependent RNA polymerase, inhibiting bacterial RNA synthesis. Acts locally in the gut lumen due to negligible systemic absorption.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to rifaximin, rifamycins, or any component
relative: Severe (Child-Pugh C) hepatic impairment (increased systemic exposure)
Diarrhea with fever or blood (suspect invasive pathogen)

preg: Use only if clearly needed; human data are limited. Animal studies showed teratogenic effects at high systemic exposures, though systemic absorption is minimal in humans.
lact: It is not known whether rifaximin is excreted in human milk; systemic absorption is minimal. Use with caution and consider benefit to the mother.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment is provided; systemic exposure is minimal because of low absorption.
hepatic: Systemic exposure is increased in hepatic impairment (highest in Child-Pugh C). Use with caution in severe hepatic impairment; however, it is specifically indicated for hepatic encephalopathy.

moderate: P-glycoprotein/OATP inhibitors (e.g., cyclosporine - increase rifaximin systemic exposure)
Warfarin (case reports of altered INR - monitor)
minor: Minimal CYP3A4 induction potential at usual exposures

rare: Severe skin reactions (exfoliative dermatitis, SJS, DRESS)

counsel: Take exactly as prescribed and complete the course
For travelers' diarrhea, stop and seek care if you develop fever or bloody stools or it does not improve in 1-2 days
Report severe or persistent diarrhea after treatment
This antibiotic acts mostly in the gut and is barely absorbed
Tell your doctor if you take blood thinners
pk: Acts locally in gut soon after dosing
Low systemic peak ~1 hour; systemic levels are minimal
Dosed 2-3 times daily depending on indication
pearls: Systemic absorption is less than ~0.4%, giving few systemic side effects and interactions
FDA-approved (Xifaxan) - distinct from many non-absorbed agents; this record is FDA-grounded
Effective add-on to lactulose for reducing hepatic encephalopathy recurrence
Not for diarrhea suspected to be invasive/inflammatory (fever, blood)
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered unless it is nearly time for the next; do not double up. Complete the full prescribed course.
overdose: No specific overdose syndrome is described; due to minimal absorption, systemic toxicity from overdose is unlikely. Management is supportive. No specific antidote.
